\chapter{Language or country?}
\label{ch:zh-language-country}
\hlchaptermodality{17}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can understand, say, read and write \zh{中文} and \zh{中国}, keep all five identity words distinct, and score listening, speaking, reading and writing separately.}

Two new identity words and the three earlier forms return at expanding intervals before separate listening, speaking, cold reading and no-model writing scores.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[zhōngwén]{Hear \emph{zhōngwén} — Chinese}

\label{lesson:ZH-C17-hear-zhongwen}



\begin{quote}
From the last chapter, say \textbf{\zh{汉语}, \zh{汉字}, \zh{字}} for \textbf{Chinese language, Chinese character, written character}. Then say the sound of \zh{中}: \emph{zhōng}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{zhōngwén} — \textbf{Chinese; the Chinese language}
\end{quote}

Keep the level first tone in \emph{zhōng}. Let \emph{wén} rise in second tone. The new second character stays hidden for now; this step is only sound and meaning.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[wén]{\zh{文} — watch four open strokes}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-wen-observe}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{go to school} as \emph{shàngxué} and write \zh{谢} once from memory. Then say \textbf{Chinese language} as \emph{zhōngwén}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — the shape}
Write \textbf{\zh{文}} in four separate strokes: top dot, horizontal bar, long fall left, long fall right. The last two strokes begin near the centre and open in opposite directions. Four strokes; three lifts.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\zh{文}} once. Say \textbf{dot, bar, left, right} as your hand moves.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E6\%96\%87.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{文}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[wén]{\zh{文} — copy with the route visible}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-wen-guided}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\zh{上学}}, say \textbf{thank you} in Mandarin, then air-write \textbf{dot, bar, left, right}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{文}} twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause after the bar and check that the two long falling strokes still open from the centre.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
From the cues \textbf{thank you} and \textbf{go to school}, say \zh{谢谢} and write \zh{上学} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E6\%96\%87.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{文}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[wén]{\zh{文} — wait, then open the two falls}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-wen-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Answer \zh{谢谢} with \textbf{\zh{不谢}}. Then look at \textbf{\zh{文}} for five seconds and cover it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say \textbf{dot, bar, left, right}, then write \textbf{\zh{文}} once without the model. Reveal it only after the fourth stroke. Repair only the first mismatch.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{you are welcome} and write \zh{不谢} without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E6\%96\%87.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{文}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[zhōngwén]{\zh{中文} — two known squares}

\label{lesson:ZH-C17-zhongwen}



\begin{quote}
Run the two-line \zh{谢谢} / \zh{不谢} exchange. Then take one Chapter 15 school-word meaning card: hear its Mandarin word, write it, read it aloud, and give its meaning. Finally say \textbf{Chinese language} as \emph{zhōngwén}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Read this before looking below:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{中文}}
\end{quote}

It joins China or middle + writing or language: \emph{zhōngwén}, \textbf{Chinese}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{中文}} once. Keep the two squares separate and let \zh{文} open at the base.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Longer return — character or language?}

\label{lesson:ZH-R17-character-language-r2}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\zh{中文}}. Write \textbf{\zh{请}} and point to its \zh{青} sound component. Then write \textbf{written character} without a model.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \textbf{Chinese character} and \textbf{Chinese language} in mixed order. Say each, read its unpointed card, then write it. Listen for the ending before choosing \zh{字} or \zh{语}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[zhōngguó]{Hear \emph{zhōngguó} — China}

\label{lesson:ZH-C17-hear-zhongguo}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{please}, then say \textbf{Chinese language} as \emph{zhōngwén}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{zhōngguó} — \textbf{China}
\end{quote}

The first syllable stays \emph{zhōng}. Change the rising ending: \emph{wén} names writing or language; \emph{guó} names a country. The new written ending waits one lesson.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[guó]{\zh{国} — frame, inside, close}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-guo-observe}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{China}. Put \zh{请} before a familiar request, then air-write the opening two strokes of a box without closing it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — the shape}
Write \textbf{\zh{国}} in eight strokes. Open the outer frame with its left side, then top-and-right. Finish every stroke of \textbf{\zh{玉}} inside. Only then add the bottom bar that closes the frame. Eight strokes; seven lifts.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\zh{国}} once. Say \textbf{frame, three bars, upright, dot, close}. Keep the bottom open until the inner dot is finished.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E5\%9B\%BD.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{国}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[guó]{\zh{国} — copy with the frame open}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-guo-guided}



\begin{quote}
Say the meaning of \zh{人} and write \textbf{\zh{汉}} once from memory. Then say \textbf{frame, inside, close}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{国}} twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause after the inner dot. Check that the outer bottom is still open; then close it with stroke eight.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
From the cues \textbf{person} and \textbf{Han}, say \zh{人} and write \zh{汉} once without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E5\%9B\%BD.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{国}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[guó]{\zh{国} — wait before closing}

\label{lesson:ZH-W17-guo-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Say what \zh{女} means. Then look at \textbf{\zh{国}} for five seconds and cover it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say \textbf{frame, inside, close}, then write \textbf{\zh{国}} once without the model. Do not uncover it until the bottom bar is complete.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{woman} and write \zh{女} without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E5\%9B\%BD.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{国}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[zhōngguó]{\zh{中国} — China in two squares}

\label{lesson:ZH-C17-zhongguo}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{son} as \emph{érzi}, then say \textbf{China} as \emph{zhōngguó}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{中国}}
\end{quote}

The shared \zh{中} is followed by \zh{国}, country: \emph{zhōngguó}, \textbf{China}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{中国}} once. In \zh{国}, finish the inner \zh{玉} before closing the bottom.

Say \textbf{the Chinese language} with the \zh{汉} beginning.
\end{quote}

\section[Practice]{Listening score — five meanings}

\label{lesson:ZH-R17-listening-five}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{daughter}, then say \textbf{Chinese language} with \zh{中} and \textbf{China}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Keep the page covered. Hear the five Mandarin words in mixed order and give the English meaning of each. Then reverse the cards and say all five Mandarin forms. Score listening and speaking separately out of five.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.

\section[Practice]{Reading score — no pinyin}

\label{lesson:ZH-R17-reading-five}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\zh{中国}} and \textbf{\zh{中文}} without saying their pinyin first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Shuffle five unpointed cards: \textbf{\zh{汉语}, \zh{字}, \zh{中国}, \zh{汉字}, \zh{中文}}. Read each cold and give its meaning. Score one point per form; pronunciation help comes only after the reading score is recorded.

Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.

\section[zì — hànzì — hànyǔ — zhōngwén — zhōngguó]{Writing score — from sound, no model}

\label{lesson:ZH-R17-writing-five}



\begin{quote}
Say what \zh{家} means. Write \textbf{\zh{家}, \zh{汉}, \zh{语}, \zh{文}, \zh{国}} without a model. Check only after all five are complete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
First say what \zh{家} means, then recover \textbf{\zh{汉}, \zh{语}, \zh{文}, \zh{国}} once from their spoken syllables. Next hear \textbf{Chinese character}, \textbf{Chinese language with \zh{汉}}, \textbf{Chinese language with \zh{中}}, and \textbf{China} in mixed order. Write all four without a model. Score the four whole words first; then repair only a missed character.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — five identity words}

\label{lesson:ZH-C17-practice}



\begin{quote}
Write \zh{家}, \zh{文}, and \zh{国} without a model, then name each aloud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. \textbf{Listening, /5:} hear all five words in mixed order and choose each meaning. 2. \textbf{Speaking, /5:} produce all five from meaning cards, with tones audible. 3. \textbf{Reading, /5:} read \textbf{\zh{中国}, \zh{汉语}, \zh{字}, \zh{中文}, \zh{汉字}} cold, without pinyin. 4. \textbf{Writing, /5:} hear all five meanings and write each form without a model.

Pass each skill separately. A miss in one column does not cancel the other three. For repair, revisit only the missed form and retry that skill.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
